sentences.text: Mesembriornis was an intermediate-sized terror bird that could grow up to 1.5 meters tall.
It was the lankiest of all terror birds, with its foot bone being 80 to 85% the length of its shin bone.
Studies estimate Mesembriornis could run at 27 m/s, a speed comparable to a modern cheetah.
Under the kicking hypothesis, the animal could deliver kicks with 3.5 times its body weight, enough to break the bones of medium-sized mammals.
The genus Mesembriornis was first described by the paleontologist Moreno in 1889.
Francisco Moreno described Mesembriornis in 1889 based on a cervical vertebra and leg bones found in Monte Hermoso, Argentina.
Mesembriornis may have broken bones to access marrow, similar to how modern bearded vultures drop bones to break them.
Mesembriornis has had several synonyms including Hermosiornis, Palaeociconia australis, and Prophororhacos.
Phylogenetic studies place Mesembriornis in a large clade that includes Procariama and Llallawavis.
Mesembriornis lived on the pampas of eastern Argentina between 5.3 and 4 million years ago.
Mesembriornis was one of the last terror birds to exist, living alongside the North American Titanis walleri.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range for Mesembriornis as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages, from 8 to 3.6 million years ago.
Scientists debate whether Mesembriornis's estimated high running speed was accurate or if its legs were primarily used for kicking prey.
